subject: health
title: Safety Signs and Safe Adults
about: Reading the signs that keep him safe (stop sign, walk and wait lights, exit, wet floor, do not enter, poison, railroad crossing), which grown-ups are safe helpers, staying put when lost, checking first before going anywhere with anyone, and learning a grown-up's phone number. NC 1.PCH.2.1 (situations that can cause injury) with 1.ICHR.1.3, 1.ICHR.1.5 and 1.ICHR.1.6 (tell a trusted adult, say no, trusted adults in the community); builds on Safe Outside.
tip: Point out signs on your next drive and let him read each one aloud before you say what it means.

cards.q: Which sign is red with eight sides?
cards.note: A shape with eight sides is an octagon. Only the stop sign has that shape.

cards.q: What does a stop sign tell every car and bike to do?
cards.note: Drivers stop, look both ways, then go. You stop at it on your bike too.

cards.q: The crossing light shows a walking person. What does it mean?
cards.note: Still look left, right and left before you step off the curb.

cards.q: The crossing light shows a red hand. Do you cross or wait?
cards.note: Wait on the curb until the walking person comes back.

cards.q: A bottle has a skull and crossbones on it. What is inside?
cards.note: You may see it on cleaners or garden sprays. Leave it alone and tell a grown-up.

cards.q: A sign says EXIT in red or green letters. What does it show?
cards.note: Exit signs glow so you can find the way out even in the dark.

cards.q: A yellow sign on the floor shows a person slipping. How do you move past it?
cards.note: A wet floor sign means the floor is slippery. Walk slowly around it.

cards.q: A sign says DO NOT ENTER. What do you do?
cards.note: A red circle with a white bar means do not go in.

cards.q: A sign with a big X says RAILROAD CROSSING. What is ahead?
cards.note: Stop, look and listen for a train. Cross tracks only with a grown-up.

cards.q: Who helps kids cross the street near school?
cards.note: The crossing guard holds up a stop sign so cars wait for you.

cards.q: You feel sick at school. Which safe adult helps you?
wrong: a person you do not know
cards.note: Your teacher can send you to the nurse.

cards.q: Which grown-ups wear a uniform and help keep people safe?
cards.note: A badge and a uniform show they are on duty to help.

cards.q: You get lost at a park. What do you do first?
cards.note: Stay put and call your grown-up's name in a big voice. They will come looking for you.

cards.q: You are lost and there is no worker around. Who is a safe grown-up to ask?
wrong: someone who wants you to go with them
cards.note: A mom or dad with children is a good helper when there is no worker or police officer.

cards.q: Someone you do not know offers candy and says, come see my puppy. What do you do?
cards.a: say no and stay with your grown-up
cards.note: Grown-ups ask other grown-ups for help, not kids. You may say no to any grown-up you do not know.

cards.q: Before you go anywhere with anyone, what is the rule?
cards.note: Check first, every time, even with people you know.

cards.q: What should you learn by heart so a helper can call home?
cards.note: Practice it like a song until you know it cold.

cards.q: Who may you tell your address to?
cards.a: a safe adult who is helping you
cards.note: A police officer, a teacher or a store worker helping you find your grown-up may need your address.
